avr-atmega328p.title: Uno R3, Nano, Pro Mini and other ATmega328P boards
upload: USB-serial chip (ATmega16U2 on a genuine Uno, CH340 or CP2102 on clones) with auto-reset through DTR; avrdude at 115200 (Uno, Nano new bootloader) or 57600 (Nano old bootloader, Pro Mini).
Pro Mini, LilyPad and bare chips need an FTDI/CH340 adapter: DTR→DTR, TX→RX, RX→TX, VCC, GND.
'programmer is not responding' / 'not in sync': wrong board or processor choice (Nano: try the other bootloader), wrong port, something on pins 0/1, or no CH340 driver on an old OS.
power: USB gives 5 V at about 500 mA; VIN or the barrel jack take 7–12 V through the regulator, which runs hot above 9 V under load.
The 3.3 V pin supplies about 50 mA (150 mA on newer Unos): not enough for an ESP-01 or any Wi-Fi module.
Motors, servos and relay coils on the 5 V pin reset the board: give them their own supply and share GND.
clones: CH340 clones need the CH34x driver on old macOS/Windows; current systems have it.
Most Indian Nano clones use the old bootloader (57600 baud); a few carry the ATmega168 (half the memory).
libraries: Servo (takes Timer1: no PWM on 9/10), LiquidCrystal, LiquidCrystal_I2C (PCF8574 at 0x27 or 0x3F), Adafruit_SSD1306 + Adafruit_GFX, DHT sensor library, NewPing or pulseIn for HC-SR04, SoftwareSerial for a second UART (one at a time, up to 57600), IRremote 4.x (IrReceiver.decode(), decodedIRData.command: the 2.x API is gone), RF24 for nRF24L01, TinyGPSPlus.
notes: Serial and the USB chip share pins 0/1: a GPS or Bluetooth module on 0/1 blocks uploads; use SoftwareSerial on other pins.
Pin 13 carries the LED, which loads the pin as an input.

avr-atmega2560.title: Mega 2560
upload: ATmega16U2 USB bridge (CH340 on clones), STK500v2 bootloader at 115200; auto-reset through DTR.
power: Same regulator and current limits as the Uno: many pins, still about 200 mA for the whole chip.
clones: CH340 Mega clones upload like the original.
libraries: Serial1 (19 RX / 18 TX), Serial2 (17/16) and Serial3 (15/14) are real UARTs: use them instead of SoftwareSerial. RAMPS 1.4 + Marlin, MCUFRIEND_kbv TFT shields, LCD keypad shields.
notes: PWM on 2–13 and 44–46; external interrupts on 2, 3, 18, 19, 20, 21 (20/21 are also SDA/SCL).
SPI is on 50 (MISO), 51 (MOSI), 52 (SCK), 53 (SS) and the ICSP header, not 10–13; shields made for the Uno's SPI pins use ICSP.

avr-atmega32u4.title: Leonardo, Micro, Pro Micro (ATmega32U4, native USB)
upload: Native USB: after reset the bootloader shows up as a different serial device for 8 s, then the sketch's own port returns; the port changing is normal.
If an upload fails, double-tap RESET (Pro Micro: short RST to GND twice) right as the upload starts; a sketch that breaks the USB stack needs this to recover.
power: 5 V/16 MHz and 3.3 V/8 MHz variants exist; a 3.3 V Pro Micro clone built as 5 V/16 MHz runs at half speed (Serial baud off by 2×).
clones: Pro Micro clones are built as Arduino Leonardo; the clone has no 11/12/13 headers, SPI is on 14 (MISO), 15 (SCK), 16 (MOSI).
libraries: Keyboard and Mouse (built in), HID-Project for more HID devices. Serial is USB CDC: while (!Serial) waits for a monitor, so remove it for standalone use. Serial1 is the UART on pins 0/1.
notes: RX/TX LEDs on PB0/PD5 (RXLED1, TXLED1 macros); analog A6–A11 sit on digital pins 4, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12.

megaavr-atmega4809.title: Nano Every, Uno WiFi Rev2 (ATmega4809)
upload: SAMD11 USB bridge programs the chip over UPDI: no button, 1200-baud touch resets it.
power: 5 V logic like the Nano; VIN 7–21 V on the Nano Every.
libraries: Servo, Wire, SPI, EEPROM, SoftwareSerial work; WiFiNINA on the Uno WiFi Rev2.
notes: Serial is USB, Serial1 the UART on pins 0/1 (unlike the classic Nano where both are the same port).

No Timer1/Timer2 registers: libraries that touch AVR timers directly (TimerOne, old IRremote, PWM tricks) do not compile; ATmega328P register code (PORTB, TCCR1A) does not apply, the megaAVR names are PORTB.OUT, TCB0, etc.

renesas-ra4m1.title: Uno R4 Minima and WiFi (Renesas RA4M1)
upload: USB DFU inside the RA4M1: if the board stops appearing, double-tap RESET (the LED fades) and upload again.
power: 5 V logic, the only 5 V 32-bit Arduino: Uno R3 shields and sensors fit. VIN 6–24 V.
libraries: WiFiS3 (not WiFiNINA) for the R4 WiFi's ESP32-S3 module; Arduino_LED_Matrix for its 12×8 matrix; Servo, Wire, SPI, EEPROM (emulated in flash), RTC, CAN, analogWave for the DAC.
notes: analogReadResolution(14) gives the full 14-bit ADC; A0 doubles as a 12-bit DAC.
The R4 WiFi's Qwiic connector is Wire1 at 3.3 V; the ESP32-S3 only does Wi-Fi/BLE, your sketch runs on the RA4M1.

samd21.title: Nano 33 IoT, MKR boards, Zero, XIAO SAMD21 (SAMD21, 3.3 V)
upload: Native USB: double-tap RESET to enter the bootloader (LED pulses) when the port is missing; normally the 1200-baud touch resets by itself.
power: 3.3 V logic on every pin: 5 V on an input destroys it. VUSB/5V pins are USB power out, not logic. MKR boards charge a LiPo from USB.
libraries: WiFiNINA (Nano 33 IoT, MKR WiFi 1010), WiFi101 (MKR1000), ArduinoBLE, Arduino_LSM6DS3 (Nano 33 IoT IMU), FlashStorage instead of EEPROM, Servo, SAMD_TimerInterrupt.
notes: 12-bit ADC (analogReadResolution(12)) and a 10-bit DAC on A0; no EEPROM (FlashStorage).
Serial is USB (while (!Serial) waits for a monitor); Serial1 is the UART on the TX/RX pins.

samd51.title: Wio Terminal, Feather M4 (SAMD51, 3.3 V)
upload: Native USB with a UF2 bootloader; double-tap RESET for the drive.
power: 3.3 V logic; 120 MHz Cortex-M4F.
libraries: Wio Terminal: Seeed_Arduino_LCD (a TFT_eSPI fork) for the screen, rpcWiFi for Wi-Fi, the buttons are WIO_KEY_A/B/C and WIO_5S_*.

nrf52840.title: Nano 33 BLE, XIAO nRF52840, Feather nRF52840 (nRF52840, 3.3 V)
upload: Native USB with a UF2 or Arduino bootloader: double-tap RESET for the drive; the 1200-baud touch resets normally.
The Arduino mbed core (Nano 33 BLE) and the Adafruit/Seeed cores are different platforms: a library written for one may not compile on the other.
power: 3.3 V logic; XIAO and Feather boards charge a LiPo.
libraries: ArduinoBLE (mbed Nano 33 BLE), Bluefruit (Adafruit nRF52 core, also XIAO through Seeed's core), Arduino_LSM9DS1 (BLE Sense) or Arduino_BMI270_BMM150 (BLE Sense Rev2), PDM for the microphone.
notes: No EEPROM: KVStore/FlashIAP (mbed) or Adafruit's InternalFileSystem. analogWrite is PWM on any pin; analogReadResolution(12) available.

rp2040.title: Raspberry Pi Pico and RP2040 boards (Arduino-Pico core)
upload: First upload: hold BOOTSEL while plugging in (a drive named RPI-RP2 appears); later uploads reset the board through USB by themselves. 'No accessible RP2040 devices in BOOTSEL mode' means do the BOOTSEL step again.
power: 3.3 V logic, not 5 V tolerant: level-shift 5 V sensors. VSYS takes 1.8–5.5 V in, VBUS is USB 5 V out, the 3V3 pin supplies about 300 mA.
clones: Purple 'Pico clone' boards with USB-C behave like the Pico; RP2040-Zero boards use GPIO16 for a WS2812 instead of a plain LED.
libraries: Arduino-Pico (Earle Philhower) core: Servo, Wire (Wire.setSDA/setSCL before begin), SPI (SPI.setRX/setTX/setSCK), Serial1/Serial2 (setRX/setTX), WiFi.h on the Pico W (not WiFiNINA), LittleFS, EEPROM emulation, Adafruit NeoPixel (PIO).
notes: Pins are GPIO numbers (GP0…GP28), not D labels; ADC on GPIO26–28 (A0–A2), the chip temperature on channel 4.
analogWriteFreq() and analogWriteRange() set PWM; every pin has PWM.
setup1()/loop1() run on the second core; rp2040.fifo passes messages. Interrupt handlers need no IRAM_ATTR (that is ESP32).

rp2350.title: Raspberry Pi Pico 2 and RP2350 boards
upload: Same BOOTSEL procedure as the Pico (the drive is RP2350).
power: 3.3 V logic, not 5 V tolerant.
libraries: Arduino-Pico core 4.0 or later; the Pico 2 W uses WiFi.h like the Pico W.
notes: Cortex-M33 (or Hazard3 RISC-V) at 150 MHz, 520 KB RAM; the pinout matches the Pico.

esp32.title: ESP32 (WROOM/WROVER dev kits, ESP32-CAM, D1 R32, LOLIN32)
upload: esptool through the USB-serial chip; dev kits enter download mode by themselves. 'Failed to connect … Wrong boot mode' means hold BOOT (GPIO0) while 'Connecting…' prints, then release. Long or thin cables: Upload Speed 115200.
Boards without a USB chip (ESP32-CAM, bare modules) upload through a USB-serial adapter with GPIO0 to GND at reset.
power: Wi-Fi draws peaks above 400 mA: a weak USB port or thin cable gives 'Brownout detector was triggered' resets; use a 5 V 1 A supply or add a 470 µF capacitor on 5 V.
VIN/5V is USB 5 V; the 3.3 V regulator (AMS1117 on most kits) has about 500 mA minus the ESP32's own use: no servos or backlit displays on 3V3.
3.3 V logic: 5 V sensors (HC-SR04 ECHO, many relay boards) need a divider or level shifter; relay boards want 5 V for the coil with a 3.3 V logic input.
clones: CH340, CP2102 and CH9102 USB chips are all common in India; CH9102 needs its own driver on old Windows.
'DevKit V1' boards differ in pin count (30 vs 36/38) between sellers but share GPIO numbers.
libraries: WiFi.h, WiFiClientSecure, HTTPClient, WebServer, ESPAsyncWebServer (+AsyncTCP), PubSubClient (MQTT), ArduinoJson, Preferences (settings), LittleFS (files), ESP32Servo (not Servo), analogWrite works (LEDC), BluetoothSerial (classic BT, original ESP32 only), BLE (built-in BLE or NimBLE-Arduino), esp_now.h, esp_camera.h on camera boards, DHT sensor library.
notes: ESP-NOW: both boards on the same Wi-Fi channel; WiFi.mode(WIFI_STA) before esp_now_init(); the receiver prints WiFi.macAddress() so the sender knows its peer (or send to the broadcast address FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF); 200 m or more line of sight.
Deep sleep wakes only through RTC GPIOs (0, 2, 4, 12–15, 25–27, 32–39): esp_sleep_enable_ext0_wakeup(); a timer wake needs no pin.
Core 1 runs setup()/loop(); xTaskCreatePinnedToCore() puts work on core 0; delay(0) or yield() inside long loops keeps the watchdog quiet.

esp32-s2.title: ESP32-S2 (Saola, LOLIN S2 Mini)
upload: Native USB (CDC) only on most boards: enable USB CDC On Boot for Serial; hold BOOT (GPIO0) while plugging in if no port appears.
power: 3.3 V logic; same brownout notes as the ESP32.
libraries: Same Wi-Fi libraries as the ESP32; no Bluetooth at all on the S2; USB device libraries (keyboard, MSC) through TinyUSB.
notes: Single core, Wi-Fi only. GPIO19/20 are USB; strapping GPIO0, 45, 46; ADC1 GPIO1–10, ADC2 GPIO11–20 (unusable with Wi-Fi); DAC on GPIO17 and 18.

esp32-s3.title: ESP32-S3 (DevKitC, SuperMini, XIAO S3, Heltec V3, T-Display-S3)
upload: DevKitC boards have two USB-C ports: the UART port (CP2102) behaves like the classic ESP32; the native port needs USB CDC On Boot for Serial (Impulse turns it on when the board is on its native port). SuperMini/XIAO boards have the native port only.
power: 3.3 V logic; brownout notes as the ESP32; the native USB port alone cannot power a camera plus Wi-Fi reliably on thin cables.
clones: DevKitC clones put the RGB LED on GPIO48 or GPIO38; SuperMini boards use GPIO48.
libraries: Same Wi-Fi/BLE libraries as the ESP32 (BLE 5 only, no classic Bluetooth so no BluetoothSerial); USB HID/MSC through the USB library; esp_camera for camera boards; TFT_eSPI for display boards.
notes: Dual core 240 MHz; GPIO26–32 are the flash and GPIO33–37 the PSRAM on octal-PSRAM (N8R8/N16R8) boards: do not use them; strapping GPIO0, 3, 45, 46; no DAC; ADC1 GPIO1–10, ADC2 GPIO11–20 (unusable with Wi-Fi). RGB LED through rgbLedWrite()/Adafruit_NeoPixel.

esp32-c3.title: ESP32-C3 (SuperMini, DevKitM-1, XIAO C3, LOLIN C3 Mini)
upload: SuperMini and XIAO boards have native USB only: USB CDC On Boot must be enabled for Serial; hold BOOT (GPIO9) while plugging in to force download mode when no port appears. DevKitC-02 boards also have a UART chip.
power: 3.3 V logic; the SuperMini's 3.3 V regulator is small (about 300 mA): no displays with backlights or servos from 3V3.
clones: SuperMini boards from different sellers: LED on GPIO8 (active-LOW) on most; some antenna layouts have poor Wi-Fi range (keep WiFi.setTxPower(WIFI_POWER_8_5dBm) in mind if the connection drops).
libraries: Same Wi-Fi libraries as the ESP32; BLE 5 (NimBLE-Arduino is lighter); no classic Bluetooth; no DAC.
notes: Single RISC-V core 160 MHz; GPIO0–21 only; GPIO18/19 are USB; strapping GPIO2, 8, 9; ADC1 GPIO0–4, ADC2 GPIO5 (unusable with Wi-Fi); UART0 TX GPIO21 / RX GPIO20.

esp32-c6.title: ESP32-C6 (DevKitC-1, SuperMini, XIAO C6)
upload: DevKitC has UART and native USB ports; SuperMini/XIAO native only (USB CDC On Boot on).
power: 3.3 V logic.
libraries: Wi-Fi 6 and BLE 5 through the usual libraries; Zigbee through the Zigbee library (needs the Zigbee partition scheme and mode in Board Options); Thread/802.15.4 through OpenThread.
notes: RISC-V 160 MHz; GPIO12/13 are USB; strapping GPIO4, 5, 8, 9, 15; ADC on GPIO0–6. Needs ESP32 Arduino core 3.0 or later: core 2.x does not know the C6.

esp8266.title: ESP8266 (NodeMCU, D1 mini, ESP-01, ESP-12 modules)
upload: esptool over CH340/CP2102 at 115200 (921600 works on good cables); NodeMCU and D1 mini auto-reset into flash mode; ESP-01 and bare modules need GPIO0 LOW at reset.
'espcomm_upload_mem failed' or 'Failed to connect': not in flash mode, wrong port, or weak power.
power: Wi-Fi peaks above 300 mA: the Uno's 3.3 V pin cannot power an ESP-01; use the NodeMCU's own regulator or an AMS1117 3.3 V module with a 100 µF capacitor.
3.3 V logic: feed a 5 V TX into RX through a divider.
clones: NodeMCU 'V3' (LoLin, CH340) and 'Amica' (CP2102) boards are both NodeMCU 1.0; the V3 is wider and has two extra pins (VU = 5 V from USB, G).
libraries: ESP8266WiFi, ESP8266WebServer, ESP8266HTTPClient, WiFiClientSecure (client.setInsecure() for quick tests), ESPAsyncWebServer (+ESPAsyncTCP), PubSubClient, ArduinoJson, LittleFS (SPIFFS is deprecated), ESP8266mDNS, ArduinoOTA, Servo, Ticker, EEPROM (emulated, 4 KB).
notes: One ADC (A0) and no DAC; PWM on any GPIO through software analogWrite (0–255 in core 3.x).
Deep sleep needs D0 (GPIO16) wired to RST: ESP.deepSleep(microseconds).
Code that blocks for about 3 s trips the software watchdog: yield() or delay(1) inside loops; the hardware watchdog resets at about 8 s.

stm32.title: STM32 Blue Pill, Black Pill, Nucleo, Discovery (STM32duino core)
upload: Tools › Upload method (Board Options): ST-Link SWD (an ST-Link V2 dongle), Serial (BOOT0 jumper to 1, USB-serial adapter on PA9 TX / PA10 RX, then BOOT0 back to 0), DFU over USB (Black Pill: hold BOOT0, tap NRST, release), Mass Storage on Nucleo boards (the onboard ST-Link acts as a drive).

Serial over the board's own USB needs USB support = 'CDC (generic Serial supersede U(S)ART)' in Board Options; otherwise Serial is the UART on PA9/PA10 (Nucleo: the ST-Link's virtual COM port on PA2/PA3).
power: 3.3 V logic; pins marked FT in the datasheet accept 5 V as digital inputs, analog pins do not.
clones: Blue Pills with CKS32F103 / CS32F103 / GD32 clone chips: an ST-Link may refuse them ('unexpected IDCODE'); use STM32CubeProgrammer (SWD) or the serial method. Some are marked C8 (64 KB) but have 128 KB.
Old Blue Pills have a 10 kΩ USB pull-up (R10) instead of 1.5 kΩ, so USB enumeration fails: add 1.8 kΩ between PA12 and 3.3 V or use ST-Link.
libraries: Servo, Wire and SPI with pin names (Wire.setSDA(PB7); Wire.setSCL(PB6); or TwoWire Wire2(PB11, PB10)); HardwareSerial Serial2(PA3, PA2); STM32duino RTC, LowPower, FreeRTOS; TFT_eSPI, U8g2 and most Adafruit libraries compile.
notes: Pins are PA0…PC15 (D0/A0 aliases exist only on Arduino-shaped Nucleo boards); LED on PC13 (Blue/Black Pill, active-LOW) or PA5 (Nucleo-64 LD2); 12-bit ADC with analogReadResolution(12); analogWriteFrequency() sets PWM.

teensy4.title: Teensy 4.0 and 4.1
upload: Teensy Loader over USB (HalfKay bootloader); press the board's button if the automatic upload does not start. The core comes from the teensy:avr board package.
power: 3.3 V logic and NOT 5 V tolerant (unlike Teensy 3.x): level-shift 5 V inputs. VIN 3.6–5.5 V; cut the VIN–VUSB pad when powering externally with USB attached.
libraries: Teensy Audio Library, IntervalTimer, elapsedMillis, OctoWS2811 and FastLED, TeensyThreads; most Arduino libraries compile.
notes: Serial is USB (always 12 Mbit/s whatever the baud); Serial1–Serial8 are hardware UARTs (Serial1 on 0/1); analogWriteResolution up to 15 bits; CPU 600 MHz by default; EEPROM emulated (4 KB).

attiny-x5.title: ATtiny85 / ATtiny84 (ATTinyCore), Digispark
upload: ATTinyCore boards program over ISP: Arduino as ISP (Uno running ArduinoISP, pins 10 RST / 11 MOSI / 12 MISO / 13 SCK, 10 µF between RESET and GND on the Uno) or a USBasp; set Tools › Programmer and use Upload Using Programmer. Digispark: Micronucleus over USB, plug the board in only after clicking Upload.
power: 2.7–5.5 V; internal 8 MHz clock by default (16 MHz PLL on Digispark); no crystal.
clones: Digispark clones work with the Digistump core; a missing driver on Windows shows them as an unknown USB device.
libraries: ATTinyCore's Wire for I2C (TinyWireM on old cores), SoftwareSerial for debug output (no hardware UART on the 85), Adafruit NeoPixel at 8/16 MHz, Servo_ATTinyCore.
notes: ATtiny85: 8 KB flash, 512 B RAM, 5 I/O pins (6 with RESET disabled, which needs a high-voltage programmer to undo); PWM on PB0, PB1 (PB4); ADC on PB2, PB3, PB4, PB5. Digispark pins P0–P5 = PB0–PB5; P3/P4 are USB (avoid while USB is in use), P1 has the LED.

attiny-modern.title: tinyAVR 0/1/2-series (ATtiny1614, 1616, 3216…, megaTinyCore)
upload: UPDI with SerialUPDI: a USB-serial adapter whose TX goes through a 4.7 kΩ resistor (or a Schottky diode) to the UPDI pin, RX straight to it; Tools › Programmer = SerialUPDI, then Upload Using Programmer. Or a jtag2updi programmer.
power: 1.8–5.5 V; 20 MHz or 16 MHz internal clock (set in Board Options; Burn Bootloader writes the fuses).
libraries: Wire, SPI, Serial (hardware UART on all 1-series parts), Servo through megaTinyCore's Servo, EEPROM (128–256 B), Logic/Event/Comparator libraries for the peripherals.
notes: Pins are PA0…PC3 with Arduino numbers from megaTinyCore's pinout chart; registers follow the new AVR style (PORTA.OUT, TCA0.SINGLE…).
